info.name: Reschedule Appointment - API Tests
info.description:
End-to-end API tests for the user story: "As a patient, I want to reschedule an existing appointment to another available time slot, without having to cancel and book from scratch."

## How to run
1. Import this collection and the environment `QA Challenge.postman_environment.json`.
2. In the environment, set `email` and `password` of the test patient. `baseUrl` is pre-filled.
3. Run the whole collection with the Collection Runner, in order. Or with Newman:
   `newman run "Reschedule Appointment - API Tests.postman_collection.json" -e "QA Challenge.postman_environment.json"`

No token needs to be pasted: the collection logs in automatically before the first request and again when the token is about to expire. Every id, date and time slot is retrieved or computed during the run. The collection creates its own test appointments and deletes them at the end, so existing data is never modified.

## Structure
- 00 Authentication: login, wrong credentials, missing or tampered token.
- 01 Setup: data needed before rescheduling (patient, doctor, available slots, a test appointment).
- 02 Reschedule happy path: reschedule, then verify the stored data, the list, notifications and availability.
- 03 Validation edge cases: missing fields, past and weekend dates, off-list and impossible times, wrong formats and types.
- 04 Business rules and security: taken slot, cancelled appointment, authentication and ownership.
- 05 Cleanup: deletes the test data and logs out.

Every response is also checked for response time, JSON content type and, on errors, the documented Error schema.

## Tests that fail on purpose
Assertions describe the expected behaviour. Tests tagged [API-xx] fail against the current API because of the defects below, found while building this collection. A failure there is a finding, not a broken test. Run with `npm run test:api` (see the repository README), failures tagged [API-xx] are reported as known defects and do not fail the build; any other failure, or a tagged test that starts passing, does.

| Tag | Defect | Related Part 1 bug |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API-01 | Reschedule response returns the appointment as it was before the change | BUG-01 |
| API-02 | updated_at is not updated on reschedule | |
| API-03 | appointment_date returned as a date-time at midnight UTC, documented as YYYY-MM-DD | BUG-02 |
| API-04 | A slot already taken with the same doctor is accepted | BUG-03 |
| API-05 | Past dates are accepted | BUG-08 |
| API-06 | Weekends and times not offered by availability are accepted | BUG-09 |
| API-07 | Malformed input accepted or answered with 500: dd/mm/yyyy is read as mm/dd when the day is 12 or less and gives 500 otherwise; Feb 30 rolls over to March; a numeric slot is stored; a non-date gives 500 | |
| API-08 | A cancelled appointment can be rescheduled | BUG-06 |
| API-09 | Cancel answers success but the status is not stored | |
| API-10 | No notification is created after a reschedule | BUG-05 |
| API-11 | Availability ignores the date and existing bookings | BUG-09 |
| API-12 | Deleting an already deleted appointment returns 200 | |
| API-13 | The token is still accepted after logout | |
| API-14 | GET /api/doctors omits is_active, documented in the Doctor schema | |
| API-15 | A notification is dated in the future (2027-03-15 in the test account) | |
